scope: Literal original receipt claims; no-sink split-K non-equality remains correctly proved. No proof-correctness, floating-point, speed or kernel-correctness assessment.

verdicts.question: S1
verdicts.basis: Inclusive-prefix skip stays strict at every later prefix and final maximum. Spec 62–70; Proofs 97–119; Primer 99–102, 248; MUTATIONS 294.

verdicts.question: S2
verdicts.basis: Final-max refinement implies prefix refinement; no equality of masks or outputs claimed. Spec 72–79; Proofs 121–145; Primer 99–102; MUTATIONS 295.

verdicts.question: S3
verdicts.basis: Containment and a valid sink-free counterexample are proved, but the receipt’s fixed sink-logit-zero counterexample is not encoded (F1). Spec 81–98; Proofs 147–214; Primer 259–261; SP1.1 report 9–13; test_apa_sp1_1.py 67–74.

verdicts.question: S4
verdicts.basis: The registered shared-prefix obstruction for 0 ≤ z ≤ √3, including both endpoints. Spec 100–113; Proofs 216–262; Primer 247; MUTATIONS 298–299; SP1 registration 115.

verdicts.question: S5
verdicts.basis: Strict true-weight certificate with full-key error bound and the 2·errq margin. Spec 115–127; Proofs 264–299; Primer 274–284; SP2 derivation 9–47.

verdicts.question: S6
verdicts.basis: S1 ADEQUATE; S2 INADEQUATE (F2); S3 ADEQUATE; S4 ADEQUATE; S5 ADEQUATE.

verdicts.question: S7
verdicts.basis: For recording all five original receipt claims verbatim. Four match; S3 certifies the sink-free variant. This does not dispute any checked proof or the qualitative split-K non-equality result.

findings.title: The split-K receipt uses sink logit 0; the Lean counterexample omits the sink.
findings.finding: The receipt fixes sink=0, which contributes exp(0)=1 to the denominator. rowOutput has no sink term. Global/split outputs in Lean are 1/(exp(2)+1) and exp(10)/(exp(2)+exp(10)); in the receipt they are 1/(exp(2)+2) and exp(10)/(exp(2)+exp(10)+1). Differences are approximately 0.8804617278 and 0.8931123035 respectively. Both exceed 0.8. Thus the qualitative non-equality claim is faithfully demonstrated, but the exact receipt construction is not machine-checked by this statement. MAJOR is about faithful recording of that fixed instance, not a false theorem or kernel defect.
findings.proposed_restatement: Retain the universal containment conjunct and the fixed bulk [2,0], exact [2,10], V [0,1], delta=0 and singleton masks. Define rowOutputWithSink(scores,V,s) = (sum_i exp(scores_i)*V_i)/(sum_i exp(scores_i)+exp(s)); use rowOutputWithSink(...,0) for both globalOut and splitOut in the >0.8 conjunct. Retain the existing no-sink theorem as an additional variant, if desired. A source-site comment should credit SP1.1 R26 (2026) and the standard softmax/sink denominator; this is a transcription repair, with no new algorithm.
findings.prior_art: APA SP1.1 (2026), R26; standard softmax normalization and online-softmax merge (Milakov and Gimelshein 2018; FlashAttention, Dao et al. 2022, via Primer section 7). Taken: receipt operands, masks and denominator semantics. New: identification of this transcription mismatch only. Literature not independently verified; unverified — lead to check: SP1.1 sink zero counterexample, online softmax Milakov Gimelshein 2018.

findings.title: sp_mask_superset_nv witnesses strictness where the claim’s antecedent is false.
findings.finding: The implication requires finalRefined b delta j. The nv statement instead requires spRefined b delta j AND NOT finalRefined b delta j. Its actual witness b=[0,1], delta=0, j=0 therefore makes the main implication vacuous at that key. This is a useful strict-containment witness, but it does not directly exercise the claim’s antecedent. This does not invalidate S2 or imply its antecedent is unsatisfiable; the same row at j=1 satisfies it.
findings.proposed_restatement: Keep the strictness existential, and conjoin a separate existential over b:Fin 2→R, delta:R and j:Fin 2 satisfying finalRefined b delta j. For example, b=[0,1], delta=0, j=1 has finalRefined and spRefined true. A source-site comment should credit SP1’s final/prefix mask containment (R24, 2026; BLASST running-max criterion, Yuan/Shinn et al. 2025/2026); this only repairs witness coverage.
findings.prior_art: APA SP1 (2026), R24, and X5 non-vacuity requirement, MUTATIONS 304–308; BLASST (Yuan, Shinn et al., arXiv 2512.12087, 2025/MLSys 2026) for the running-max criterion, via Primer section 7. Taken: existing mask definitions and antecedent-satisfiability requirement. New: diagnosis that strictness and antecedent coverage differ. Literature not independently verified; unverified — lead to check: BLASST running maximum criterion.

definitions.name: prefixMax
definitions.check: Spec 25–27: nonempty finite supremum of b over i ≤ j; includes j; no artificial zero. For [-2,-3], prefixes are [-2,-2].

definitions.name: rowMax
definitions.check: Spec 29–31: maximum of all eligible row keys; Fin(n+1) is nonempty, including n=0. No sink is a key in this maximum.

definitions.name: localPrefixMax
definitions.check: Spec 33–35: maximum over P ∩ {i ≤ j}; hj includes j and ensures nonemptiness. Arbitrary finite subsets generalize ordered partitions; no singleton-only restriction. Empty partitions have no j to decide.

definitions.name: spRefined
definitions.check: Spec 37–39: signed bulk ≥ inclusive prefix maximum − δ. Equality refines; negation gives strict skip. All real δ generalizes the receipt’s nonnegative margins.

definitions.name: finalRefined
definitions.check: Spec 41–43: signed bulk ≥ final row maximum − δ; distinct from both the z rule and the prefix rule.

definitions.name: mixedScores
definitions.check: Spec 45–47: exact on refined keys, bulk otherwise; all keys retained.

definitions.name: rowOutput
definitions.verdict: MISMATCH for the fixed R26 instance
definitions.check: Spec 49–51: correct scalar sink-free softmax, strictly positive denominator. A scalar output suffices for an output-inequality counterexample. Omits the sink-zero denominator contribution in the cited receipt (F1).

definitions.name: zRefined
definitions.check: Spec 53–60: moments of absolute bulk, population variance, max(var,0), mean+z·sqrt, inclusive threshold; N=n+1 is the count of eligible keys.

z_rule_comparison.check: Spec 12, 56–59: interpret Fin(n+1) as exactly the eligible causal prefix or full row, n+1=s_max>0. Masked keys are not zero-filled into N.
b_i is the scaled bulk dot; moments use |b_i| and |b_i|², including negative scores by magnitude.
Each key counted once; WCOOP lane-zero gate avoids 32-fold duplication. mean=Σ|b|/N; var=Σ|b|²/N−mean², population rather than sample variance.
mean + zthr·sqrt(max(var,0)) equals Spec 60 in real arithmetic. Variance is nonnegative mathematically; retaining the clamp matches the code.
|bulk| ≥ threshold refines, with equality included; otherwise bulk is retained. Matches zRefined and mixedScores.

For A=[1,0,0,0], μ=1/4, var=3/16, threshold=(1+z√3)/4. At z=0 it is 1/4; at z=√3 it is exactly 1, so key 0 refines at both. For B=[1,0,0,10], μ=11/4, var=283/16; threshold≥11/4>1 for z≥0, so key 0 skips.

The interval [0,√3] contains the receipted zthr=1.0364333894937898. At each fixed z and row length, any deterministic decision based only on the identical observed prefix induces the same f(1); both masks cannot be matched. The first three values coincide, so waiting through those zeros also cannot distinguish the rows. No unrestricted buffering impossibility or result for every real z is certified.
